issues.description: The problem statement and the template define the addParent method as addParent(Person person, Person parent) (child first, parent second), but the solution implementation declares the parameters in reversed order (addParent(Person parent, Person person)). Although the parameter types are identical (both Person), the swapped parameter positions change semantics: callers (e.g., PersonResource and the tests) pass (child, parent), but the solution method treats the first argument as the parent and the second as the person, resulting in inverted relationship updates. This mismatch between the intended signature/semantics and the solution implementation is structural and will confuse students and cause incorrect behavior when wiring the REST resource to the service.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the addParent method signature and parameter order with the problem statement and template: declare and implement addParent(Person person, Person parent) (person/child first, parent second) and update internal parameter names accordingly. Alternatively, if the solution intentionally swaps the order, update PersonResource and tests to call the service with the matching argument order — but the preferred fix is to restore the (person, parent) order to match the specification and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define and refer to the service method as addParent(Person person, Person parent) (child first, parent second). In the solution, PersonService.addParent is declared with the parameter identifiers in reversed order (public Person addParent(Person parent, Person person) — effectively swapping the conceptual roles). This parameter naming/order mismatch between the artifacts creates a cognitive mapping barrier: students reading the problem and template will expect the first parameter to be the child and the second the parent, but the solution's parameter naming suggests the opposite, which can confuse understanding and debugging (and may hide subtle semantic errors when comparing implementations).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution's method signature and parameter names with the problem statement and template: declare addParent as public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent) and implement it using 'person' as the child and 'parent' as the parent (e.g., check person.getParents(), add parent to person.getParents(), then save and return person). Ensure any callers (PersonResource, tests) pass arguments in the same child-then-parent order.
